```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
if (identical(Sys.getenv("DRMTMB_CMR_SOURCE"), "true")) {
  devtools::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
} else {
  library(drmTMB)
}
```

`drm_cjs()` fits a fixed-effects Cormack–Jolly–Seber model conditional on each
animal's first capture. The survival formula models logit unit-time apparent
survival. Over an interval of length `Delta`, survival is `phi_unit^Delta`; the
detection formula models detection conditional on being alive and surveyed.
This route does not estimate abundance or unseen animals.

## Fit a model

```{r fit}
y <- rbind(
  c(1, 0, 0, 0), c(1, 0, 1, 0), c(1, 1, 0, 0), c(1, 1, 1, 0),
  c(1, 0, 0, 1), c(1, 0, 1, 1), c(1, 1, 0, 1), c(1, 1, 1, 1)
)
d <- cmr_data(y, id = seq_len(nrow(y)), occasions = 1:4, units = "years",
              frequency = c(12, 4, 8, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4))
fit <- drm_cjs(d, phi = ~1, p = ~1)
coef(fit)
```

## Predict and simulate conditionally

Training predictions return only keyed interval and occasion rows that
contribute to the objective.

```{r predict}
pred <- predict(fit)
head(pred$phi)
head(pred$p)
```

Simulation retains the observed first-capture times, survey masks, and
administrative endpoints. It conditions on the first-capture emission and
keeps death absorbing. Supplying a seed gives reproducible data without
changing the caller's random-number stream.

```{r simulate}
simulated <- simulate(fit, nsim = 1L, seed = 20261006)[[1L]]
refit <- drm_cjs(simulated$data, phi = ~1, p = ~1,
                 phi_data = simulated$phi_data, p_data = simulated$p_data)
coef(refit)
```

## Inspect fixed-effect intervals

Wald and profile intervals use the CJS-specific observed likelihood curvature
and constrained CJS refits, respectively. The parametric bootstrap retains
every attempt and its status. Results expose a status for each coefficient.
These methods have not passed the programme's separate recovery and coverage
qualification, so available intervals do not establish nominal calibration.

```{r intervals}
ci <- confint(fit, method = "wald")
attr(ci, "target_status")
```

The current implementation covers fixed-effects CJS. Shared and persistent
individual effects, predictor-dependent random-effect standard deviations,
and reference-cohort selection correction are later programme stages.
